thread:
Alex: Quick sync — we need a lightweight playbook for bringing a dormant region online on-demand for large tenants without violating residency rules. Idea: an autoscale+warmup path that preloads model KV and cache for a specific tenant, marks traffic as 'local-preferred' once warm, and keeps audit logs for residency. Thoughts?
Maria: +1. Need to be explicit about the data flow: what gets copied vs what stays control-plane-only. Also how we record consent.
Sam: Tradeoffs: warmed region reduces latency but risks duplication of writes if we try to accept resident writes before we have final replication. We should avoid synchronous cross-region commit during warmup. Prefer localbuffer -> async-ship with replay window.
Julie: Runbook idea (operator POV): 1) mark tenant eligible 2) run warmup job 3) promote routing hint 4) monitor perf & errors 5) rollback. Can we make each step idempotent?
Kevin: Metrics to track: warmup_duration, cache_hit_rate (tenant), buffered_write_count, async_ship_lag_ms, residency_audit_events. Add an alert if buffered_write_count > X for > Y minutes.
Alex: Good list. Also need config knobs exposed in tenant config: "region_activation_mode" (auto/manual), "warmup_topk", "accept_writes_while_warming" (deny/buffer/accept-readonly).
Maria: Prototype config snippet for discussion:
```json
{
  "region_activation_mode": "auto",
  "warmup_topk": 2000,
  "accept_writes_while_warming": "buffer",
  "async_ship_max_batch_ms": 2000
}
```
Sam: Important to call out semantics: if buffer mode, client gets 202 accepted and we surface a short-lived write_id. We should document idempotency keys and replays. Also costs bump for tenant during warmup — communicate to billing.
Julie: Operator commands (sample):
```
# kick a warmup for tenant-42 into eu-west
redwoodctl region warmup --tenant tenant-42 --region eu-west --force
# abort and drain
redwoodctl region warmup --tenant tenant-42 --region eu-west --abort
```
Kevin: For legal/residency audit, we need an immutable event: "region_activation:tenant-42:eu-west:ts" plus a fingerprint of the cache state (hash of top-k keys). Keep in audit logs for retention policy.
Alex: Failure scenarios: 1) warmup fails partially (cache primed but model kernels mismatch) -> route back to origin region and mark tenant as degraded for X hours. 2) warmup completes but async ship lag > SLO -> operate in read-local, write-buffer for a grace period. Need automatic rollback.
Maria: Also consider capacity prebook model: large customers can reserve cold-slices (reserved GPUs kept at minimal scale) to reduce warmup time. This is a commercial option vs fully on-demand.
Sam: Consistency model doc blurb: during warmup we switch to "eventual-accept" semantics for writes with guaranteed replay ordering by sequence numbers. Consumers must handle transient 202 + write-id pattern.
Julie: UX: show tenant state in Console: Idle / Warming / Active-local / Active-remote / Degraded. Include ETA and buffered write gauge.
Kevin: OpsBot: deploy canary for warmup controller to staging?
OpsBot: deploy-bot: canary warmup-controller promoted to staging at 1714210000 — https://ci.redwood/warmup/1234
Alex: Next steps: Maria to draft RFC + sample runbook, Julie to write operator checklist, Kevin to propose alerts and retention for audit events. Sam will write the write-buffer API spec. I'll coordinate the canary.
Maria: I can take RFC first pass by EOD tomorrow. Will include cost, consistency, and privacy sections.
Julie: I'll draft the runbook after RFC so we can reference exact command semantics.
Sam: I'll stub the API with examples (202 payloads, replay endpoints) and add integration tests.
Alex: Awesome — thanks. Tag me once RFC is ready, we'll fast-track a short review. :thumbsup:
